overview: Nekoware v1 private's Stealer is a near byte-for-byte port of the Memeware 7.3 module with one renamed mode and one dead branch: it registers Normal and Aura modes, but the empty-chest close condition still tests isMode("Nearby"), which can never match, so the mode-based auto-close is dead code and only the Close setting closes the chest. The steal loop is otherwise identical: one shift-click per Delay ticks through the fork's windowClick (pure C0E, no C09 sync), C0D close through EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen, and an Aura-mode chest scan that swings with C0A and opens chests with C08. The Delay 0 divide-by-zero crash is inherited from the shared modulo gating.

sections.p: The file differs from its Memeware sibling in exactly three lines: the package, the mode registration (Nearby renamed to Aura) and the unchanged isMode("Nearby") test in the empty-chest close branch. The Aura branch itself works, because the scan condition tests isMode("Aura") against the registered string, but the close condition's Nearby test never matches, so in Aura mode an emptied chest closes only when the Close setting is on. That asymmetry, a renamed mode leaving a stale string test behind, is the kind of copy-paste drift that identifies a port: the developer renamed the mode string in the registration but missed the consumer.

The steal loop matches the sibling exactly: with a GuiChest open, the module shift-clicks the first occupied slot whenever ticksExisted modulo the rounded Delay is zero, one item per click, and calls mc.displayGuiScreen(null) when the first 27 or 54 slots are empty and the Close setting permits. The Aura mode scan runs with no screen open, walks a 7x7x7 box, and for each unlisted chest within distance-squared 16 sends C0APacketAnimation and right-clicks it open via onPlayerRightClick, which emits the C08. The emptied list clears on every S08PacketPlayerPosLook after terrain load and on enable.

The fork's PlayerControllerMP.windowClick queues only C0EPacketClickWindow and never syncs the held slot, so the drain is pure C0E traffic with no C09, and the module never switches held items. The close emits C0D through the fork's EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen, and the Aura open emits C0A plus C08. The tick-modulo pacing gives 5 C0E per second at the default Delay of 4, 20 per second at Delay 1, and a crash at Delay 0, since ticksExisted modulo zero throws. The S08 consumer is receive-side and only resets the chest set.

files.label: Stealer.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is two registered consumers plus the isEmpty helper, identical in shape to the Memeware port. eventConsumer0 runs the open-chest steal loop and the Aura scan, eventConsumer1 clears the emptied list on S08 teleports, and isEmpty counts occupied slots among the first 27 or 54. The Delay setting gates every click through the tick modulo, which is the module's rate control and its crash edge at zero.\n\nThe register line for modes is where the port diverges: "Normal" and "Aura" are registered, but the close branch tests isMode("Nearby"), a string that no longer exists, so that branch is dead and the Close boolean is the only working auto-close path. The import of the lwjeb @Handler registration wires the consumers to the UpdateEvent and PacketInEvent buses, and the class holds no timers, buffers or packet construction of its own.

files.label: PlayerControllerMP.java (fork window protocol)
files.explanation: The fork's PlayerControllerMP defines every packet the module puts on the wire. windowClick computes the container's next transaction id, runs slotClick locally to get the clicked stack, and queues a single C0EPacketClickWindow; it never calls syncCurrentPlayItem, so window clicks carry no C09 held-item sync, a fork fingerprint identical to the Memeware sibling. onPlayerRightClick is the chest-open path: for an activated block it queues the C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the position, facing and held stack that the Aura mode triggers.\n\nThe module calls only windowClick and onPlayerRightClick, so this one file accounts for the entire C0E and C08 footprint. The C0D close comes from the fork's EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen rather than this class, and the C0A swing is sent directly by the module. The file is byte-identical to the Memeware 7.3 fork version, which is expected of a port and is what makes the two stealers wire-identical.

countering.label: FastClick (window click rate)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus FastClick scores InventoryClickEvent traffic into an ActionFrequency with five 200ms buckets: the newest bucket is compared against the short-term limit of 4 and the full window against the normal limit of 15, with TickTask lag division before the comparison. A plain shift-click with an empty cursor counts 1.0 via getAmountWithAction. The check also carries the container-interaction path: any click landing within the 155ms min-interaction-duration default after the container opened adds a violation of (155 / duration) * 100, and slot -999 throws are excluded entirely.\n\nThe stock configuration is the honest gap: Delay 4 is exactly 5 clicks per second, one per 200ms bucket and 5 across the window, safely under both limits, so a default drain passes the rate paths. The pressure comes from the dial and the open: Delay 1 raises the rate to 20 per second, blowing the 15 window (about 5 VL per click, cancel at vl>150 within about 1.5 seconds), and the first click always lands within a frame of the chest opening because there is no first-delay setting, so the interact_time path scores close to 100 VL on every drain regardless of the delay. The module's tick-modulo pacing is rigid, which is exactly what a bucket check is built to fingerprint.

countering.label: Open (inventory close on movement)
countering.explanation: NCP's Open check watches PlayerMoveEvent traffic while an inventory window is open. checkOnMove skips duplicate packets, vehicles, creative quickbar clicks, merchants and velocity-affected moves, then decides whether the move carries an impulse: with modern input it reads the WASD/jump bits directly, otherwise it falls back to the movement model's hasImpulse decision. An impulse while open feeds Improbable and returns true, and the caller force-closes the inventory, resetting inventoryOpenTime and containerInteractTime.\n\nThe module suppresses nothing, so any strafing or stepping during a drain is visible to the check and a single impulse move mid-steal closes the chest and aborts the session. The practical tension is the same as every stealer: a still player never trips it, so the check is a soft counter that converts a movement mistake into a lost window and resets the open-time baseline FastClick's interact_time path reads. The Aura mode's walking between chests happens with no window open and is invisible to it.

countering.label: InventoryActions (window state mismatch)
countering.explanation: Hawk's InventoryActions punishes world interaction while a window is open and, more importantly for stealers, punishes ClickInventoryEvent packets when HawkPlayer.hasInventoryOpen() is zero. Hawk derives the open state from the S2D window-open, C16 inventory command and close packets, so it tracks the server's window lifecycle, not the client's GUI state, and every punish calls e.resync().\n\nThe module's close-then-reopen cadence is the race surface. The empty-chest branch calls mc.displayGuiScreen(null), which queues C0D, and in Aura mode the next delay tick can immediately right-click another chest and swing; if Hawk has not yet processed the C0D, the C0A swing and C08 open arrive while hasInventoryOpen is still non-zero and are punished and resynced. The reverse edge is equally live: a click that lands after the server-side close processed arrives with the window flag at zero and is punished as a click on a closed window. The dead isMode("Nearby") close branch does not change this, because the Close setting still drives the C0D cadence.

countering.label: FastConsume (eat-duration; silent for stealers)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's FastConsume guards the item-use path of the inventory family. The inventory listener stamps a consume time on the right-click of an edible or potion, and the check compares it against the consume-time limit (1280ms default) when PlayerItemConsumeEvent fires, flagging any consume that completes faster than a real eat could. The mechanism only engages when a consume event actually lands, which requires the full vanilla use duration to elapse.\n\nFor this module the check is silent by design: shift-click C0E traffic, the C0D close and the Aura C08 opens never produce a consume event, so FastConsume stays quiet through an entire drain. The entry belongs in the set because the same C0E corpus pools the eat-rate checks with the click-rate checks, and it documents the boundary honestly: the real pressure on this module is FastClick's click ledger, while FastConsume is the guard for the instant-consume sibling modules, which would trip it on any server that processes eats immediately.
